literal: Than poverty it is painful, wealth, justice who-does-not-do king's scepter under if it falls.
translation: If one falls under the scepter of a king who does not administer justice, possessing wealth is more painful than poverty.
modern: நீதி வழங்காத அரசனது ஆட்சியின் கீழ் வாழ நேர்ந்தால், வறுமையை விடச் செல்வம் உடையவராக இருப்பதே ஒருவருக்கு அதிகத் துன்பத்தைத் தரும்.
explanation: This couplet highlights the extreme insecurity of living under a tyrant. The phrase 'இன்மையின் இன்னாது உடைமை' states a paradox: having wealth is actually more painful than being in poverty. This happens when one's life falls under the scepter ('கோல்') of a king who does not govern justly ('முறைசெய்யா மன்னவன்'). Under such an unjust rule, a wealthy person becomes a constant target for extortion and confiscation, living in perpetual fear, whereas a poor person has nothing for the tyrant to steal.
